chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Do not spend the nights of Al-Tashreeq except in Mina. So if you spend the nights in other than it, then upon you is blood (of a sacrificial animal). And if you leave on the first night, the middle of the night should not pass for you unless you are in Mina, unless your occupation is with your rituals, or you have left from Makkah. And if you leave after the middle of the night, it does not harm you if you see the morning in other than it.

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a man who visited (the Kaaba) in the evening. So he did not cease to perform his Tawaf, supplicate, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, until the dawn emerged. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him. He was in the obedience of Allah.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to the sacrificial animal (dam) required as a penalty
key_terms.لَيَالِيَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The nights of Al-Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on spending the nights of Tashreeq in Mina and what are the exceptions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the mandatory nature of staying in Mina during the nights of Al-Tashreeq, prescribing a sacrificial animal (dam) as a penalty for those who depart early without valid excuse, such as engaging in ritual duties or leaving Makkah. It further clarifies that prolonged devotion through Tawaf, Du'a, and Sa'i until dawn is considered an act of obedience and incurs no penalty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual obligation with spiritual devotion. The ruling underscores the historical practice of the Imams regarding the logistics of Hajj and the flexibility granted to pilgrims engaged in worship.
